name: toyota_4a_ge
label: Toyota 4A-GE 1.6 L 16-valve inline-four (AE86)
based_on: Toyota 4A-GE first generation (big port, T-VIS), European specification without catalyst (10.0:1), AE86 Corolla GT, 1983 on

sources.what: Austrian Toyota Corolla 1600 Coupe GTi brochure (Toyota importer Ernst Frey OHG, dated 20.11.83), 'Technische Beschreibung': 4A-GE, 1587 cc, bore and stroke 81.0 x 77.0 mm, compression 10.0, 91 kW / 124 DIN-PS at 6600 rpm, 142 N m at 5200 rpm, D-Jetronic manifold-pressure injection. Factory-distributed sales literature, scanned on an enthusiast club site.

Toyota, 'All About the Toyota Twin Cam' (1984, English edition, scanned on 3sgte.com), pages 11 and 14-15: T-VIS (two runners per cylinder, one closed by a butterfly at low and mid speeds), 4A-GEU specification table, 50-degree valve angle, four valves, forged crankshaft, and a full-load curve (Japanese gross rating) used only as a shape guide. Manufacturer publication.

Ate Up With Motor, AE86 history part 3: European 4A-GE at 10.0:1 without catalytic converter, 124 PS DIN and 142 N m; 7500 rpm redline. Part 2 (same site) gives T-VIS opening at 4650 rpm. Researched automotive history.
Third-party reproduction of 1986 US Corolla Sport RWD 4A-GE service data: firing order 1-3-4-2, cylinder 1 at the front. The same site gives base idle 800 rpm. Not a Toyota page.

Bill Sherwood's 'Stock 4AGE' pages (enthusiast, archived 2012): 29.5 mm intake and 25.5 mm exhaust valves, big-port cam timing 9/51/51/9 degrees, 240 degrees, 7.56 mm lift; page 2: 55 mm throttle, 4-2-1 exhaust manifold, T-VIS at 4400 rpm. No references given.

Club4AG camshaft chart: stock AE86/AW11 cams 240 degrees, 7.56 mm, intake opens 9 BTDC, exhaust opens 51 BBDC, Toyota part numbers 13501-16010 / 13502-16010. Enthusiast source; agrees with the page above.
Tomei aftermarket rod set for the 4A-G(Z), listed at 122.00 mm. Search-result title only; weak source for the stock rod length.

notes: Modelled variant: the first-generation 'big port' 4A-GE with T-VIS in its European form (no catalytic converter, compression 10.0:1, manifold-pressure injection), rated 91 kW (124 PS DIN) at 6600 rpm and 142 N m at 5200 rpm in Toyota Austria's November 1983 brochure for the AE86 Corolla 1600 Coupe GTi. It is chosen because that is the only rating found that is net, gives both peak speeds and comes with its own compression ratio in one factory-distributed document; the Japanese 4A-GEU's 130 PS is a gross figure, and no opened page gave the US engine's torque speed. Sourced from Toyota documents: bore 81.0 mm, stroke 77.0 mm, 1587 cc, compression 10.0, four valves per cylinder, published power and torque, T-VIS described as two runners per cylinder with one of each pair closed at low and mid speeds. Sourced from non-Toyota pages: firing order 1-3-4-2 with cylinder 1 at the front and idle 800 rpm (a third-party reproduction of 1986 US service data), redline 7500 rpm (used as the limiter; the fuel-cut speed was not found), valve diameters 29.5 and 25.5 mm, cam timing 9/51/51/9 degrees with 7.56 mm lift on both cams, 55 mm throttle and a 4-2-1 exhaust manifold (enthusiast pages that agree with each other but cite nothing). A flat-plane crank is assumed (the only layout that gives the sourced order with even firing). Pairing cylinders 1+4 and 2+3 in the 4-2-1 manifold is assumed. Estimated, not sourced: rod length 122 mm (an aftermarket rod listing), the lift at which the cam timing is quoted (0.25 mm assumed; the sources do not say, and this choice moves the result: quoting the same angles seat to seat gives about 7 percent more torque at 5200 rpm and an earlier power peak), intake runner length and diameter, header primary and secondary lengths and diameters, exhaust pipe diameter, plenum, airbox, mufflers and tail pipe (derived defaults), flywheel inertia (derived default). Fit: the cam reference lift, runner length, and heat_q 2.4e6 were tuned, with friction_scale 0.9, against the published peaks and against the shape of Toyota's own full-load curve for the Japanese engine (a gross curve, used only for its shape: torque at 2000 rpm about 81 percent of peak, flat from 5000 to 5600, about 94 percent at 6500). The model is flatter than that curve at low speed (about 89 percent of peak at 2000 rpm). Not modelled: T-VIS. The definition format has one fixed runner per cylinder, so the runner diameter (42 mm) stands for both runners of each pair open, which is the state above the opening speed (quoted as 4200, 4400 or 4650 rpm by different sources; no Toyota figure found), where both published peaks lie. Below that speed the real engine draws through one runner of each pair, for more air speed and swirl; the model does not, and it has no change of intake note at the opening point. The air-flow meter of US engines is not part of this variant.

vehicle.name: Toyota Corolla 1600 Coupé GTi (AE86, Austria, 1983)
vehicle.notes: All values from the Austrian Toyota brochure of November 1983 for the three-door 'Coupé GTi' with the 124 DIN-PS European engine. The weight is the brochure's 'Eigengewicht'; the brochure does not say whether a driver is included. wheel_radius_m is my calculation from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.
